The free tier has limits on speed and file size.
- **About 30 messages per second** to different users and **about one message per second** to a single chat. In groups a bot sends up to 20 messages per minute.
- **A broadcast to 10,000 subscribers** takes around six minutes at these limits. For most businesses this is enough.
- **Files:** a bot downloads files up to 20 MB and uploads up to 50 MB through the standard Bot API.
The file limit is removed with your own Bot API server. Telegram publishes its code for free, and with it a bot uploads files up to 2 GB. You pay only for the hosting.

Developers withdraw Stars through Fragment at $0.013 per Star, paid in Toncoin. A Star can be withdrawn 21 days after it was received, and the minimum withdrawal is 1,000 Stars.

### Is the Telegram API free?
Yes. The Bot API, the Telegram API (MTProto) and TDLib are free. Telegram does not charge for a bot token, for requests or for the number of users.
### Does the Bot API have a paid plan?
There is no subscription. The only paid part of the Bot API itself is paid broadcasts: 0.1 Stars per message above about 30 messages per second, for bots with at least 100,000 monthly active users.

title: Is the Telegram Bot API Free? Official Pricing, Fees & Limits (2026)
snippet:
**Quick answer: Yes, the Telegram Bot API is free.** Telegram charges no fees to create a bot, call the API or send messages — there are no paid tiers and no per-message costs, and the official Bot API documentation lists no pricing. Your only costs are running the bot (hosting, database) and optional extras like [Telegram Stars](https://aziqdev.com/blog/telegram-stars-explained) payments and paid broadcasts. The API does have [rate limits](https://aziqdev.com/blog/telegram-bot-api-rate-limits) — about 30 messages per second overall and 1 per second per chat.
The Telegram Bot API is completely free. No monthly fee, no per-request charge, no paid tier upgrade. But if you search for "Telegram bot API pricing" and expect a simple answer, you will find the question is more nuanced: **the API is free, but running a production bot has real ongoing costs** — and those costs catch many builders off guard.

FREE
### Telegram Bot API
$0/month
The Bot API gives your bot the ability to send messages, receive updates, manage groups, handle payments, serve inline queries, and interact with Telegram's full feature set. There is no paid plan, no API key pricing tier, and no per-message fee.
**Rate limits (not paid, just enforced):**
- 30 messages per second to different users
- 20 messages per minute to the same group
- No documented limit on incoming updates
These limits are soft throttles, not hard paywalls. You cannot pay to increase them. Design your bot to respect them.

## Free Hosting Options (With Trade-offs)
Several platforms offer free tiers that work for development and low-traffic bots:
- **Railway (free tier):** 500 free hours/month — enough for a bot running 16 hours/day. $5/month for always-on.
- **Render (free tier):** Free web services that spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity. Polling bots work; webhook bots spin down between messages. Fine for personal projects.
- **Fly.io (free tier):** 3 shared VMs free. Better for always-on bots than Render.
- **Oracle Cloud Free Tier:** Permanently free ARM VMs (2 vCPU, 12 GB RAM). Best free production option — no credit card spin-down issues.
